name: Jaipur
short_intro: The 'Pink City', a meticulously planned 18th-century capital of forts, palaces and a rooftop astronomical observatory.
overview: Jaipur was founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, a keen astronomer, and laid out on Vastu Shastra planning principles as one of India's first grid-planned cities, later painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales. The hilltop Amber Fort, City Palace's courtyards, and Hawa Mahal's honeycomb façade of 953 windows built for royal women to observe street life unseen all reflect the Kachhwaha rulers' blend of Rajput and Mughal architectural taste. Jantar Mantar, the largest of Jai Singh's five observatories, still functions as a working stone-and-marble astronomical instrument.

attractions.name: Amber Fort
attractions.description: A hilltop fort-palace with mirrored halls, reached by jeep or elephant ride.

attractions.name: Hawa Mahal
attractions.description: A pink sandstone façade of 953 small windows, built for royal women's private street views.

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.description: The former royal residence, still partly home to the Jaipur royal family.

attractions.name: Jantar Mantar
attractions.description: A UNESCO-listed stone astronomical observatory with the world's largest sundial.

culture.summary: Jaipur is a centre of Rajasthani miniature painting, blue pottery, gemstone cutting and traditional puppet (kathputli) performance.

festivals.name: Jaipur Literature Festival
festivals.description: One of the world's largest free literary festivals.
festivals.significance: A major modern cultural draw alongside the city's heritage.

festivals.name: Teej
festivals.description: A monsoon festival celebrated with processions honouring Goddess Parvati.

food.name: Dal Baati Churma
food.description: Baked wheat balls with lentils and a sweet crumble, Rajasthan's signature meal.

food.name: Laal Maas
food.description: A fiery red mutton curry from the Rajput hunting tradition.

food.name: Ghewar
food.description: A disc-shaped syrup-soaked sweet especially made for Teej.

travel_info.bus: Well connected across Rajasthan and to Delhi/Agra.
travel_info.local_transport: Autos, cabs and the Jaipur Metro.

tips: Bargain at bazaars like Johari and Bapu Market.
Book Amber Fort elephant rides only through official counters.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; tourist police active near major sites.

name: Delhi
short_intro: Layered capital of Mughal monuments, colonial avenues, and Sultanate-era ruins spanning eight historic cities.
overview: Delhi has been the seat of power for successive empires for nearly a millennium, and the city wears every layer of that history at once. Qutub Minar's Indo-Islamic tower rises from 12th-century ruins; Humayun's Tomb prefigures the Taj Mahal's garden-tomb design; Lutyens' colonial avenues frame Rashtrapati Bhavan; and Old Delhi's Chandni Chowk still runs the food and trade routes laid out by Shah Jahan. Modern Delhi adds Akshardham's carved sandstone and the Lotus Temple's petalled concrete to that timeline.
best_time_to_visit: October to March; summers exceed 40°C and the monsoon is humid.

attractions.name: Qutub Minar
attractions.description: A 73-metre 12th-century minaret and UNESCO World Heritage Site marking the start of Indo-Islamic architecture in India.

attractions.name: Humayun's Tomb
attractions.description: A Mughal garden-tomb built in 1570 that directly inspired the Taj Mahal's design.

attractions.name: Red Fort
attractions.description: Shah Jahan's red-sandstone Mughal citadel, site of the annual Independence Day flag-hoisting.

attractions.name: Chandni Chowk
attractions.description: A 17th-century bazaar street famous for street food, wedding-wear shopping and spice trading.

culture.summary: Delhi blends Mughal-era Urdu poetry and cuisine with Punjabi post-Partition energy and a modern political-capital cosmopolitanism.

festivals.name: Republic Day Parade
festivals.description: A grand military and cultural parade down Rajpath.
festivals.significance: Marks the adoption of India's constitution.

food.name: Chandni Chowk Paranthe
food.description: Stuffed fried breads served in a century-old lane dedicated to them.

food.name: Butter Chicken
food.description: Tomato-and-cream chicken curry, invented in Delhi's Moti Mahal in the 1950s.

food.name: Chaat
food.description: Tangy, spiced savoury snacks like golgappa and aloo tikki sold citywide.

travel_info.railway: New Delhi, Old Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations.
travel_info.bus: ISBT terminals connect across North India.
travel_info.local_transport: Delhi Metro covers most tourist areas.
travel_info.budget: Budget to premium; wide range available.

tips: Use registered taxis or the Metro at night.
Air quality worsens in winter — check AQI.

name: Kurukshetra
short_intro: The legendary battlefield of the Mahabharata, where the Bhagavad Gita was said to be recited, centred on the sacred Brahma Sarovar tank.
overview: Kurukshetra is revered as the site of the Kurukshetra War described in the Mahabharata and the setting where Krishna is said to have delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna. The town's spiritual geography centres on Brahma Sarovar, one of the largest and holiest water tanks in India, ringed by ghats and temples. The Jyotisar shrine marks the exact spot linked to the Gita's recitation.
best_time_to_visit: October to February; the Gita Mahotsav runs in November-December.

attractions.name: Brahma Sarovar
attractions.description: A vast sacred tank considered one of the holiest bathing sites in Hindu tradition.

attractions.name: Jyotisar
attractions.description: The site traditionally identified as where the Bhagavad Gita was recited.

attractions.name: Sannihit Sarovar
attractions.description: A tank believed to be visited by all sacred rivers during solar eclipses.

culture.summary: Kurukshetra's identity is built entirely around Mahabharata mythology, drawing pilgrims and scholars of the epic year-round.

festivals.name: Gita Mahotsav
festivals.description: A month-long cultural and spiritual festival around Brahma Sarovar.
festivals.significance: Celebrates the Gita's teachings with music, dance and discourse.

food.name: Bajra Khichdi
food.description: A hearty millet-and-lentil dish typical of rural Haryana.

food.name: Lassi
food.description: Thick churned-yoghurt drink served everywhere in the region.

travel_info.bus: Well connected to Delhi, Chandigarh and Ambala.
travel_info.local_transport: Autos and taxis around the tank circuit.

tips: Crowds swell heavily during Gita Mahotsav.

name: Amritsar
short_intro: Home to the golden-domed Harmandir Sahib and the nightly patriotic spectacle at the Wagah border.
overview: Amritsar is Sikhism's holiest city, built around the Golden Temple, whose gold-plated sanctum sits amid a marble courtyard and sacred pool, the Amrit Sarovar. The temple's free community kitchen serves over 100,000 people daily regardless of faith. A short drive away, the Wagah border ceremony turns India-Pakistan flag lowering into a roaring nightly show, while Jallianwala Bagh preserves the memory of the 1919 massacre.
best_time_to_visit: October to March; summer is very hot.

attractions.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
attractions.description: Sikhism's holiest gurdwara, gold-plated and set in a sacred pool.

attractions.name: Wagah Border
attractions.description: The India-Pakistan border ceremony with synchronized drills and crowds cheering both sides.

attractions.name: Jallianwala Bagh
attractions.description: A memorial garden marking the 1919 massacre site, a turning point in the independence movement.

culture.summary: Amritsar embodies Sikh values of seva (selfless service) and langar (community kitchen), alongside a robust Punjabi culture of music, food and hospitality.

festivals.name: Baisakhi
festivals.description: Punjab's harvest and Khalsa-founding festival celebrated with Bhangra and Gidda.
festivals.significance: Marks the Sikh new year and Khalsa formation.

food.name: Amritsari Kulcha
food.description: Stuffed leavened bread baked in a tandoor, a city signature.

food.name: Makhi Fish
food.description: Punjabi-spiced fried river fish, an Amritsar specialty.

food.name: Langar Prasad
food.description: Simple communal meal served free at the Golden Temple to all visitors.

travel_info.airport: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport (ATQ).
travel_info.bus: Frequent buses across Punjab and to Delhi/Chandigarh.
travel_info.local_transport: Autos and cycle-rickshaws around the old city.

tips: Cover your head and remove footwear at the Golden Temple.
Arrive early for Wagah border seating.
etiquette: No smoking, alcohol or leather items inside the Golden Temple complex.

name: Srinagar
short_intro: Kashmir's summer capital, built around Dal Lake's houseboats and Mughal terraced gardens.
overview: Srinagar sits on the banks of the Jhelum river and around Dal Lake, where cedar-wood houseboats and shikara boats have hosted travellers since Mughal times. The Mughal emperors laid out terraced gardens like Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh specifically to enjoy the valley's scenery, and that legacy of leisurely, garden-framed beauty still defines the city, alongside a strong handicraft tradition in wood-carving, papier-mâché and Kashmiri shawls.
best_time_to_visit: April to October; snowfall closes many roads in winter.

attractions.name: Dal Lake
attractions.description: The iconic lake with houseboats, floating gardens and shikara rides.

attractions.name: Shalimar Bagh
attractions.description: A Mughal terraced garden built by Jahangir for Empress Nur Jahan.

attractions.name: Hazratbal Shrine
attractions.description: A white-marble mosque on Dal Lake's shore holding a relic of the Prophet.

culture.summary: Kashmiri culture blends Persian-influenced Sufi traditions with distinct cuisine, poetry and one of India's finest handicraft traditions.

festivals.name: Tulip Festival
festivals.description: Asia's largest tulip garden blooms at the foot of the Zabarwan hills.
festivals.significance: A modern festival celebrating spring in the valley.

food.name: Rogan Josh
food.description: A slow-cooked, deep-red lamb curry central to Kashmiri Wazwan.

food.name: Kahwa
food.description: Saffron-and-almond spiced green tea served throughout the valley.

travel_info.railway: No direct rail; nearest is Jammu Tawi, then road.

tips: Check current travel advisories before planning.

name: Leh
short_intro: The high-desert capital of Ladakh, ringed by Buddhist monasteries and some of the world's highest motorable passes.
overview: Leh sits at over 3,500 metres in a stark Trans-Himalayan desert, its old town climbing toward the ruined Leh Palace beneath the Namgyal Tsemo monastery. It is the springboard for Ladakh's dramatic geography: Pangong Lake's blue expanse, the Nubra valley's sand dunes, and passes like Khardung La among the highest roads on earth. Tibetan Buddhist culture runs deep, from prayer-flag-strung ridgelines to butter-lamp-lit monasteries.
best_time_to_visit: May to September; passes are snowbound the rest of the year.

attractions.name: Leh Palace
attractions.description: A 17th-century royal palace overlooking the old town, modelled on Lhasa's Potala Palace.

attractions.name: Shanti Stupa
attractions.description: A white-domed Buddhist stupa with panoramic Leh valley views.

attractions.name: Pangong Lake
attractions.description: A vast high-altitude lake changing colour through the day, straddling the India-China border area.

culture.summary: Ladakhi culture is rooted in Tibetan Buddhism, with monastery festivals, mask dances and a resilient high-altitude farming tradition.

festivals.name: Hemis Festival
festivals.description: A masked-dance festival at Hemis Monastery marking Guru Padmasambhava's birth.
festivals.significance: One of Ladakh's largest monastic festivals.

food.name: Skyu
food.description: A hand-shaped pasta-and-vegetable stew suited to the cold climate.

food.name: Butter Tea
food.description: Salted, buttered tea essential at altitude.

travel_info.railway: None; nearest is Jammu Tawi, far by road.
travel_info.local_transport: Taxis and hired bikes; permits required beyond Leh.

tips: Rest a day or two in Leh before higher altitudes.
Inner Line Permits required for Pangong, Nubra and Khardung La.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; medical facilities are limited outside Leh.

name: Chandigarh
short_intro: India's first planned city, laid out by Le Corbusier in strict grid sectors around Sukhna Lake and the Rock Garden.
overview: Chandigarh was conceived after Partition as a fresh capital for Punjab, designed from scratch by Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier with wide avenues, numbered sectors and modernist civic buildings. Nek Chand's Rock Garden, built secretly from industrial and household waste over decades, sits in striking contrast — a folk-art sculpture park within a rationalist city. Sukhna Lake offers a calm morning-walk counterpoint.

attractions.name: Rock Garden
attractions.description: A sprawling sculpture garden made entirely from recycled waste and rocks by artist Nek Chand.

attractions.name: Sukhna Lake
attractions.description: A man-made lake at the foothills of the Shivaliks, popular for boating and walks.

attractions.name: Capitol Complex
attractions.description: Le Corbusier's UNESCO-listed government buildings, a landmark of modernist architecture.

culture.summary: Chandigarh's identity is defined by deliberate urban planning and a relaxed, orderly Punjabi-inflected lifestyle rare among Indian cities.

festivals.name: Chandigarh Carnival
festivals.description: A citywide cultural and food festival.
festivals.significance: Celebrates the city's founding and civic identity.

food.name: Chole Bhature
food.description: Spiced chickpeas with fried bread, a North Indian staple widely available here.

food.name: Sector 17 Street Food
food.description: A concentrated food-stall scene in the city's central plaza.

travel_info.bus: ISBT Sector 43 connects across Punjab, Haryana and HP.

tips: Sectors follow a grid; note your sector number to navigate easily.

name: Mathura-Vrindavan
short_intro: Krishna's legendary birthplace and childhood playground, twin temple towns alive with devotional colour, especially at Holi.
overview: Mathura is revered as Krishna's birthplace, marked by the Krishna Janmabhoomi temple complex, while nearby Vrindavan is where he is said to have spent his childhood among the gopis, celebrated in temples like Banke Bihari and ISKCON's Krishna-Balaram Mandir. The twin towns form the heart of the Braj region's devotional culture, reaching a peak at the exuberant, colour-drenched Holi celebrations that draw pilgrims from across the world.
best_time_to_visit: October to March; Holi (Feb-March) is the biggest, most crowded draw.

attractions.name: Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple
attractions.description: A temple complex marking Krishna's traditional birthplace.

attractions.name: Banke Bihari Temple
attractions.description: Vrindavan's most visited Krishna temple, famous for its unusual curtain-based darshan ritual.

attractions.name: ISKCON Krishna-Balaram Mandir
attractions.description: A major International Society for Krishna Consciousness temple and pilgrim hub.

culture.summary: Braj culture centres entirely on Krishna devotion, expressed through Raslila dance-dramas, temple rituals and the region's famous Holi festivities.

festivals.name: Holi
festivals.description: Days of colour-throwing celebrations across Mathura, Vrindavan and Barsana.
festivals.significance: Celebrates Krishna's playful colour games with Radha and the gopis.

festivals.name: Janmashtami
festivals.description: Krishna's birthday, marked with midnight celebrations and temple decoration.
festivals.significance: The most important festival in the Krishna devotional calendar.

food.name: Peda
food.description: Mathura's famous milk-based sweet, sold in shops across the old town.

food.name: Kachori-Sabzi
food.description: Fried lentil-stuffed bread with spiced potato curry.

travel_info.bus: Frequent buses from Delhi and Agra.

tips: Holi crowds are intense; guard belongings.
Footwear must be removed at all temples.
